stories.title: Stunning Collection of Stolen Greek Artifacts Spanning 5,000 Years Were Just Returned to Greece
stories.label: world
stories.summary: A huge collection of ancient Greek treasures, some going back 5,000 years, has just been sent home to Greece. The pieces, including two bronze helmets, ancient armor, and a marble bust of a Roman emperor, had been stolen and ended up in New York, some even on display at the Met. Investigators tracked them down and authorities made the call to return them to their rightful home. It's a reminder that pieces of history, no matter how long they've been missing, can still find their way back where they belong.
stories.why_good: Real stolen cultural heritage was recovered and physically repatriated, restoring history to the people it belongs to.

stories.title: Chinese Commercial Reactor Achieves Nuclear Fusion with Clean Hydrogen-Boron Fuel
stories.label: science
stories.summary: Engineers in China just pulled off something remarkable: they briefly achieved nuclear fusion using hydrogen and boron as fuel, a combination that's far cleaner and more abundant than what's typically used. An independent international team reviewed the results and called it a real, meaningful step forward for fusion energy. This matters because hydrogen-boron fusion produces almost no radioactive waste, making it an exciting path toward safer, limitless clean power down the road. It's a small but genuine breakthrough in the decades-long quest to harness the same energy that powers the sun.
stories.why_good: A real, verified scientific achievement that advances clean energy technology, independently reviewed and confirmed as significant.

stories.title: Genetic Analysis All But Confirms the Most Unique of Humpback Populations Is Actually a Subspecies
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: Scientists have confirmed something pretty special: the humpback whales living in the Arabian Sea are so genetically distinct from their cousins elsewhere that they count as their own subspecies. These whales stay in warm tropical waters year-round instead of migrating, which makes them unique in the whale world. This discovery helps conservationists understand exactly how rare and precious this small population is, so they can protect it properly. It's a reminder of how much wonder is still being uncovered in our oceans.
stories.why_good: A real scientific finding that deepens our understanding and protection of a rare whale population, with no disaster or suffering at its core.
